scheme_name: Financial Assistance on Death/Disablement of Beneficiary (CBOCWWB)
description:
The Financial Assistance on Death/Disablement of Beneficiary scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India.

This scheme is specifically designed to provide financial support to the families of construction workers in the event of death or disablement.

The scheme was launched under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act of 1996.

The primary objective of this scheme is to ensure that the families of construction workers do not face financial hardships due to the loss of their breadwinner.

The scheme aims to provide timely financial assistance to the dependents of construction workers who have died or become disabled while working.

The assistance amount is set at ₹2 lakh in the event of death.

In cases of permanent disablement, the assistance amount is ₹1 lakh.

The scheme targets construction workers who are registered under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker.

The applicant must have been actively engaged in construction work at the time of the incident leading to death or disablement.

The applicant must also have a valid registration number issued by the respective State Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The age limit for eligibility is generally between 18 years and 60 years.

The income criteria for eligibility is set at a maximum of ₹15,000 per month.

This income limit is applicable to the construction worker at the time of registration.

The application process for this scheme is straightforward and involves several steps.

First, the applicant must obtain the application form from the local office of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The application form can also be downloaded from the official website of the respective State Welfare Board.

The applicant must fill in the required details accurately.

The following documents are required to be submitted along with the application form.

A copy of the death certificate or disability certificate issued by a competent authority.

A copy of the registration certificate of the construction worker.

Proof of relationship to the deceased or disabled worker must also be provided.

This can include documents such as an Aadhaar card or a ration card.

Once the application form and documents are ready, the applicant must submit them to the local office of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The application must be submitted within 90 days of the incident leading to death or disablement.

Upon submission, the application will be verified by the officials of the Welfare Board.

The verification process typically takes about 30 days.

If the application is approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed within 15 days.

The disbursement is made directly to the bank account of the eligible beneficiary.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

Each state has its own Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board responsible for the implementation of this scheme.

For example, the Maharashtra Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board oversees the implementation in Maharashtra.

The contact details for the Maharashtra Board can be found on their official website.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to enhance the welfare of construction workers.

According to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, there are over 50 million construction workers in India.

Many of these workers are engaged in unorganized sectors and lack social security benefits.

The introduction of this scheme aims to bridge the gap in social security for these vulnerable workers.

The scheme also aligns with the government's goal of providing social security to all workers in the unorganized sector.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is crucial for families who may lose their primary source of income.

The scheme has been operational since its inception and continues to evolve based on the needs of construction workers.

The government periodically reviews the scheme to ensure it meets the requirements of the beneficiaries.

In recent years, there has been an increase in awareness about the scheme among construction workers.

This has led to a rise in the number of registrations with the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

As of 2023, it is estimated that over 10 million construction workers are registered under this scheme.

The government has also initiated outreach programs to educate workers about their rights and benefits under this scheme.

These programs are conducted in collaboration with various non-governmental organizations.

The outreach efforts have been particularly focused on rural areas where many construction workers reside.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have availed of the financial assistance.

Many families have reported that the assistance has helped them cope with the financial burden following the loss of a family member.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of construction workers.

It provides a safety net for families during times of crisis.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of registration for construction workers.

Registered workers are entitled to various benefits under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Act.

The government encourages all construction workers to register with their respective state boards.

This registration not only provides access to financial assistance but also to other welfare schemes.

The Financial Assistance on Death/Disablement of Beneficiary scheme is a critical component of the social security framework for construction workers in India.

It plays a vital role in ensuring that the families of construction workers are supported in times of need.

The scheme is a reflection of the government's efforts to improve the living standards of workers in the unorganized sector.

Overall, the Financial Assistance on Death/Disablement of Beneficiary scheme is an essential welfare initiative that provides much-needed support to the families of construction workers in India.
